title: Projectile Motion
body:
**Projectile motion** is two-dimensional motion under gravity alone, with air resistance
ignored. It works because the horizontal and vertical components are independent: gravity acts
downward, so it changes the vertical velocity and leaves the horizontal velocity constant.

```
launched at 20 m/s, 30° above the horizontal, g = 9.8 m/s²

  vₓ = 20 cos 30° = 17.32 m/s     constant for the whole flight
  v_y = 20 sin 30° = 10.0 m/s     changes at -9.8 m/s²

  time to return to launch height:  t = 2v_y/g = 2.04 s
  range:                            vₓ t = 17.32 × 2.04 = 35.3 m
  maximum height:                   v_y²/2g = 5.1 m
```

The horizontal direction uses constant-velocity motion and the vertical uses
[[Uniformly Accelerated Motion]], and time is the one quantity shared between them,
which is how the two halves are joined.

At the peak the vertical velocity is zero and the horizontal velocity is unchanged, so the
projectile is still moving and is still accelerating downward at $9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$. A ball
dropped from a height and a ball fired horizontally from the same height land at the same
moment, since their vertical motions are identical, and that is the demonstration worth holding
on to because it is the independence of the components made visible.
